news.title: Remedy Boss Reacts After Control Resonant Sells 1 Million Copies, Becoming Studio's Fastest-Selling Game
news.summary: Control Resonant has sold one million copies, becoming Remedy’s fastest-selling game in spite of leakers crack

others.title: Control Resonant sells 1 million copies in 3 weeks to become Remedy's fastest-selling game ever

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/10/controlthumb-1789054804916.png
Control Resonant has sold one million copies, becoming Remedy’s fastest-selling game in spite of leakers cracking the title and pirating it after its digital launch in September.
Remedy celebrated this milestone on October 15, writing on Twitter/X, “Thank you for the support. For playing, sharing, and being a part of the community.”
Remedy’s communications director Thomas Puha also commented on this achievement, saying, “There we go. Strong start.”
There we go. Strong start.

This means that Control Resonant has soared past Alan Wake 2 , which previously held the record for the studio’s fastest-selling title. The legacy sequel reached one million copies sold two months after its release; Control Resonant has achieved that figure in just three weeks.

This is welcome news for both Remedy and fans of the game, many of whom urged players against downloading the pirated version of the title when it launched digitally in late September. It seems this wasn’t a crippling setback for the developer, though, given its current financial success — and physical editions of the game have just now been released, so there’s still more profit to be had.

Control Resonant was met with critical acclaim among both reviewers and players alike. We at IGN scored it an eight out of 10 , with reviewer Michael Higham saying, “Even when combat's sharp edge eventually dulls, Control Resonant is a great addition to the Remedyverse. While its story follows a more standard framework, its gravitational pull is in the inventive world built around it and the humanization that grounds the paranatural intrigue.”
In fact, the game was so good that many internet pirates decided against illegally downloading it, choosing instead to support Remedy in the hopes that its success would help keep the studio alive.

"One of the very few games I'm going to be buying, Remedy are on the brink of bankruptcy, this is their make or break title, I love their games and gotta do what I can to keep them afloat," wrote one fan on a piracy subreddit.
"I wasn't planning to buy it but now I feel like I should," another said. "I like Remedy. They do good games."

Remedy is known for titles like the original Control game, Alan Wake 2, Max Payne , and Quantum Break . And while their offerings have been met with high praise from players, they aren’t necessarily tailored for mass appeal, leaving some gamers worried about the developer’s future — but if these latest figures are anything to go by, it seems to be faring just fine.

news.title: Pro Dota 2 Player Claims He Had to Play a Full Match in Front of Police Officers to Prove His Identity
news.summary: A pro Dota 2 player is claiming he had to play a full Dota match in front of police officers to prove his iden

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/15/kez-1792100791294.jpg
A pro Dota 2 player is claiming that he had to play a full Dota match in front of police officers to prove his identity.

According to Nuengnara "23savage" Teeramahanon, who currently plays hard carry for Xipto eSports, the team’s boot camp in Kuala Lumpur was raided by police earlier this week. In a post to Facebook on Tuesday, 23savage describes the police placing the team in handcuffs and confiscating their belongings.

The officers proceeded to interrogate the players about why they were in the city and whether they were really pro players. According to 23savage, one of the officers was familiar with Dota, and was willing to scroll the player’s Instagram for proof of his pro career.

A photo 23savage had recently posted of himself and popular Malaysian influencer Ms. Puiyi was, according to the post, somewhat acceptable evidence. Enough evidence, in fact, for the police officers to remove his handcuffs and test what really mattered: how good he is at defending the ancients.

23savage proceeded to start up a Dota match right in front of the police officers, dropping 32 kills as the hard carry Kez. The Dota player alleges that this was enough proof to convince the officers to let the team go, and also that they stole two jars of Nutella on their way out.

Commenters on the post quickly doubted 23savage’s claims, presuming the post to be a joke, but 23savage has been actively defending his story in the replies. Reddit users continue to doubt the hard carry player, while others jokingly claim 23savage’s story is saving Valve’s MOBA.

The incident doesn’t seem to have had much impact on Xipto, who have been climbing the ranks of SEA Dota. The team recently won the EPL SEA tournament without losing a single series, achieving an impressive 10-match win streak. The team’s full roster currently consists of 23savage (Carry), inYourdreaM (Mid), Fbz (Offlane), Q (Support), and Oli (Support), who are now competing for a spot in the DreamLeague Season 30 tournament .

Dota 2 itself has been seeing some notable player gains in 2026, having recently hit its peak player count since 2022 . The game continues to receive occasional patches and content updates, though Valve's focus is largely now on a new MOBA: Deadlock .

news.title: Less than 2 weeks after announcing RuneScape Reignited, Jagex is scrapping the whole thing
news.summary: In the wake of a furious backlash from players, Jagex admits it "missed the mark."

others.title: RuneScape Reignited Canceled Less Than Two Weeks After Being Announced

content.v: Life comes at you fast, as the saying goes, and the folks at RuneScape developer Jagex can sure attest to that. Less than two weeks after announcing RuneScape Reignited —essentially a way for new and lapsed players to restart their adventures from fresh on separate, unique servers—the studio has decided to cancel it.

There was trouble with RuneScape Reignited almost right from the start, with complaints ranging from a potential community split to restrictions on character interactions and the need to pay for a separate subscription. Just a few days after the initial announcement, Jagex apologized for making veteran players feel like they were being shunted aside, and said it was "exploring a heavy set of revisions to Reignited based on your feedback."

A few days after that, it laid out a more specific list of intended alterations , and invited more feedback from players, "so we can follow up next week with more of our thoughts." With that feedback now received, it seems that Jagex has heard enough. "It is clear that we missed the mark on this, and so we are not moving forward with it," Mod Ryan—associate creative director Ryan Philpott—said in a blog post announcing the cancellation. "Our goal is to see Runescape grow again, with returning players coming back and new players joining, but never at the expense of our existing community."

It's a very sudden about-face, but not unprecedented. In 2023, for instance, Jagex dropped a new RuneScape battle pass in the wake of massive player backlash; in 2025, the studio scrapped "Treasure Hunter" microtransactions , in what Jagex CEO Jon Bellamy said was "part of a wider transformation across Jagex, which is seeing a renewed commitment to delivering deeper value, greater fairness and long-term improvements for players."

It hasn't been entirely smooth sailing: Recent price hikes have not gone over well (no surprise there, though), and Jagex's cowardly decision to scrap in-game Pride Month events was allowed to stand despite players absolutely mauling the studio for it. But in terms of gameplay, at least, Jagex has demonstrated a willingness to react with relative haste when it's blown things sufficiently badly—and this definitely qualifies.

Despite the cancellation, Philpott invited new and returning players to jump into the game with a 10 day free trial beginning on December 2, which will offer full access to all worlds and content. The 2027 roadmap for RuneScape also remains in place:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/HxePPyPTPiDdBLSHB3VfHM-1920-80.jpg

"The future of RuneScape is still extremely bright," Philpott concluded. "RuneScape will always be built for and defined by its community. So please keep letting us know when you feel we're getting it wrong and shout with that same energy when you think we're getting it right too."

news.title: Street Fighter review roundup: sorry, folks, but it sounds like a mess
news.summary: The general consensus seems to be that Street Fighter isn't a disaster, but it definitely misses a lot more th

content.v: I had such high hopes for the Street Fighter movie: The trailers were so promising, the cast so charismatic, and it seemed to get the inherent ridiculousness of the franchise, playing it seriously without ever really taking it too seriously. I mean, you don't put a guy like David Dastmalchian in the role of M. Bison unless you expect him to do something with it, right?

Alas, it seems that this may be a real Tuesday , at least for my Street Fighter movie aspirations. The reviews are in, and they are not especially kind. Street Fighter isn't a complete catastrophe, according to the critical consensus, but I don't think JCVD has to worry about having to turn in his "Best Street Fighter Movie" trophy anytime soon, either.
Here's what they're saying:
"Dumber than a box of rocks, but have you ever thrown rocks at things? It can be pretty fun"

The story is too thin to support its bloated roster, but IGN reckons the Street Fighter film is "all about landing as many punches as it can before the round timer hits zero. Even though there are plenty of misses, the ones it does manage to land hit hard."
"A garish and incoherent mess that amuses in fits and starts but barely improves on the Mortal Kombat movies before it"
The Guardian : 2/5

Fans might enjoy the new SF flick, and the performances are "likeable," but its repeated self-knowing acknowledgment of how silly it all is "would land better if the movie ever rose above the stuff it’s making fun of. Instead, Street Fighter is satisfied punching down on itself, and everything that’s cringe about the '90s, while happily being stuck there, in the past, so it could pretend that this is as good as it gets for videogame adaptations."
"Not a great adaptation of what is one of the most recognizable brands in all of gaming"
Collider : 6/10

"The movie is at its most fun when it truly locks in for those high-octane fights and the surprisingly beautiful and not-much-publicized animated sequences," Collider reviewer Aidan Kelley wrote. "Unfortunately, to get to those, you have to deal with a lot of exposition and unengaging character drama."
"One of the most overtly mixed bags of any movie this year"
ScreenRant : 7/10

Despite calling Street Fighter "a fundamentally flawed movie on an underlying storytelling level," ScreenRant's review is one of the more positive takes floating around out there: The film is "buoyed by the overall 'go for broke' tone" and director Kitao Sakurai's "great work helming the film, working with the cast and crew to deliver consistently entertaining fight scenes that are flush with personality and style."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/7AEvKY9uAw3kAc522RUdQc-1920-80.jpg
"Like a trip to a ’90s mall arcade, Street Fighter’s pretty fun — for about 30 minutes"
ScreenCrush : 5/10

"The sheer absurdity and fevered intensity of the pacing, not to mention some very athletic fight choreography, is good enough to carry things along through the jittery first act," reviewer Matt Singer wrote for ScreenCrush. "But you can only mainline caffeine for so long before it starts to give you a headache."
"A campy '90s nostalgia ride and a complete mess"
Associated Press : 1/4

Street Fighter is a "very enthusiastic, weirdly convoluted and jumbled mess of a movie," Jake Coyle wrote for AP. As much as you might think a Street Fighter movie, good or bad, would at least offer up some bluntly entertaining hand-to-hand combat, it’s so messily plotted and chaotically conceived that it makes a game with six buttons seem comparatively artful."
"Dull fight scenes and tonal whiplash make this mostly forgettable videogame adaptation work only for superfans"
The Film Verdict

Street Fighter "is a little bit of everything that amounts to a lot of not-much," The Film Verdict declared, comparing it unfavorably to this year's Mortal Kombat and Resident Evil flicks: Street Fighter has all the elements that made those films successful, "but never lands on a formula than functions."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TemaybzeHpFVorpFjtMon9-1920-80.jpg
"I’m not sure Street Fighter meets any conventional standard of quality, but it’s undeniably its own thing"
The Wrap

This review takes a more holistic approach to Street Fighter, calling it "an action-packed, hyper-stylized, borderline-nonsensical fever dream with a central storyline that begs to be taken seriously" despite being goofy, horny, largely incoherent, and somehow "even weirder" than the 1990s movie. But hey, maybe that's your thing: As reviewer William Bibbiani wrote, "What even is a 'good movie' anyway?"
"A jumbled tonal mess that feels deadly serious one moment and like parody the next"
The Hollywood Reporter

"Featuring so many characters and elements from the games that non-aficionados are left desperately attempting to keep up, Street Fighter tries to thread the needle between fan service and welcoming the uninitiated," THR says. "The result is that neither camp is likely to be fully satisfied."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/sfTe253Q4iGfinopcVdMZ-1920-80.jpg
"Not even close to coherent, but it does have some good fight scenes"
Gizmodo

Gizmodo's review says the Street Fighter film is a bit like its portrayal of Ken Masters, an oafish clown who can actually fight: "The editing choices, scene transitions, and even the basic plot are frequently baffling. And yet, it can throw a punch when it wants to."
"The closest any filmmaker has come to bringing the franchise’s signature verve and bombast to the big screen"
Inverse

In another relatively positive review, Inverse declares that "Street Fighter might not be a film that sticks in your brain for days afterwards, but while you’re in your seat it feels like a shot of adrenaline to the arm, the kind that you might get from hearing the coveted 'You Win' announcement after the end of a hard-fought match."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/HCfj9eghzaAFWKedhbTr5n-1920-80.jpg
"Something goes terribly awry in its back half, hinting at either a troubled production, or one that was doomed from the start"
Variety

Variety was impressed by Street Fighter's strong start, but says the wheels come off in the second half: "It’s a film at war with itself, in which a straightforward narrative about strained brotherhood is spread far too thin across unconnected snippets of action and comedy that grow increasingly disparate."

So there you have it: Not a disaster, but definitely a mess. We'll hopefully have our own critical take on the Street Fighter film up eventually, if we can ever talk Mollie Taylor into going to see it; in the meantime, if you've seen it, let us know what you think.

The Galaxies Autumn Showcase 2026 has arrived, and it featured exciting reveals for over 50 games, including Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, The Finals, InZOI, and many more.

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Launch Trailer Has Us Even More Excited to Jump In

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse is available now on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch, and PC, and the Galaxies Autumn Showcase revealed its launch trailer and now we are even more excited to start playing!
The Finals' Prime Time Season Is Shaping Up to Be Something Special

My Penguin Friend is coming soon to PC.

Feed Monsters With Your Friends in One More Plate!

One More Plate! will be released on PC on November 10, 2026.
Guns of Eschaton Is a First-Person Soulslike Action Shooter Set in an Apocalyptic Western World

Guns of Eschaton will be release on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC on December 8, 2026.

Become a Clockwork Toy Who's Ready for a Taste of Freedom

Lelu, the upcoming action-adventure monochromatic exploration game developed by Jamierowan, will be coming to Nintendo Switch 2 and PC on January 21, 2027. Get ready to become a concious clockwork toy who's ready for a taste of freedom.
Gravity Circuit 2 Gets a Demo and Slick Trailer

Mega Man X fans should take note of Gravity Circuit 2, the upcoming 2D action platformer sequel developed by Domesticated Ant Games. As a new Ark emerges, playerrs can embody Gravity or Power Circuit when the game arrives in Spring 2027. To help with the wait, a demo is now available on Steam.
Voidwood Gets a Playtest on Steam

Steam players can check out the pre-alpha playtest of Voidwood, the upcoming 1-4 co-op survival horror game where proximity voice chat is part of the danger. Players must communicate to survive, but teh Beast is always listening.

The acclaimed PC shooter, Squad , is coming to consoles — and PS5 players will be able to experience it very soon.

Developer Offworld Industries has announced that Squad will be making its way to Xbox Series X|S and PS5. The PC version of the game launched in 2020, and it has been one of the more beloved tactical shooters on Steam for some time. Before Wardogs ever came into the picture, Squad attempted to strike a balance between the milsim nature of Arma with the more fast-paced action of more mainstream shooters like Call of Duty or Battlefield.

It'll be interesting to see if Squad can beat Wardogs to consoles. Bulkhead has already announced that Wardogs will hit consoles in 2028 and recently told IGN that expects the game to also have a port on next-gen hardware, when it becomes available. news.title: Why Rockstar Canceled Its PlayStation-Exclusive Follow-Up To GTA 4
news.summary: At E3 2009, Sony announced that it was partnering with Rockstar on a PlayStation-exclusive spy game called Age

content.v: At E3 2009, Sony announced that it was partnering with Rockstar on a PlayStation-exclusive spy game called Agent , with Rockstar founders Sam and Dan Houser overseeing development. The game never materialized, though, and now Dan Houser has shared more details as to why.

Speaking to IGN , Houser said Agent never coming out shouldn't be a total shock because he worked on "a bunch of games that never came out." He said Rockstar tried with two or three different teams to make Agent--an open-world spy game--but the teams just "could not get it right."
"And it never came out. We concluded that it was not a game we were ever going to figure out how to make. Other people can try, but I personally think it's hard," he said.
Great spy movies like the James Bond series work so well because they take viewers all over the world, but "that's not an experience in an open-world game that really works," Houser said.
"So we tried lots of things and couldn't get it quite right," Houser said, going on to say that the teams built great elements but they never came together in a full package.
Images of Agent, which was reportedly set in the '70s, have emerged over the years, showing off some of what Rockstar was planning.
In 2009, then-Take-Two president Ben Feder told GameSpot that Agent was being positioned to be the next Grand Theft Auto .

“It’s the A team working on an AAA title,” he said at the time. “I think the subject matter, the characters, the story, the environment, the background–all the elements are there. It’s such a rich environment to play in.”
Across the industry, games get canceled regularly-- Blizzard has said it cancels 50% of the games it starts --but Rockstar's Agent got more traction because of the studio's profile.

Rockstar never gave Agent a release date, but it would have followed up 2008's Grand Theft Auto 4. The next game that Rockstar North led development on after GTA 4 was 2013's GTA 5, and now Rockstar North is set to release GTA 6 on November 19.

news.title: Activision Confirms Brand New Call of Duty Subfranchise Is in the Works, Leading to Rampant Fan Speculation
news.summary: Activision is actively developing a new Call of Duty subfranchise, suggesting it is ready to move on from Blac

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/05/27/cod-mp-preview-br2-1779914695480.jpg
Activision is actively developing a new Call of Duty subfranchise, suggesting it is ready to move on from Black Ops and Modern Warfare for the time being.

In a new interview with The Game Business , Activision's Chief Marketing Officer, Tyler Bahl, confirmed that one of its studios is developing a new Call of Duty subfranchise. Although Bahl didn't state which studio is making it or when it would release, it is widely believed this will be the next game from Sledgehammer Games, expected to release next year. He also noted that Modern Warfare 4 will conclude the story that Infinity Ward has been telling since 2019, but suggested that universe could continue in the future with certain characters.
However, Activision believes the path forward for Call of Duty is less about leaning on legacy franchises and familiar faces, and more about innovation.

“Where we go with future games, we have to innovate," said Bahl. "What we heard from the audience is they want new or better or different. The landscape is changing right under our feet. You’re seeing new games being built overnight, and you’re seeing tastes change and how people want to play.”

These comments have led to all kinds of speculation about where the next Call of Duty game will go. Will they try to go into the future? The far-flung past? What kind of mechanic can they introduce to make it feel fresh without changing things up too much? Well, a rumor from Call of Duty leaker TheGhostofHope in 2025 may provide some insight, assuming it pans out.

The rumor suggests that Sledgehammer's next game will have a focus on martial arts, with karate kicks and karate chops. It's possible that Sledgehammer is trying to lean into John Wick's gun-fu combat, which mixes satisfying gunplay with fluid, flashy close-quarters combat. That seems more doable for a third-person game with a heavy emphasis on animations, but a first-person, fast-paced, competitive game may have a harder time implementing that kind of gameplay. If it works out, it could be really compelling, though.

Interestingly enough, Sledgehammer Games really began its tenure as a Call of Duty team by trying to innovate. The studio was built with the expectation that it would develop a third-person Call of Duty game set in the Vietnam War, attempting to leverage the team's experience on games like Dead Space to create a new kind of Call of Duty experience. That project was eventually killed as Sledgehammer was pulled in to help develop the original Modern Warfare 3 after Infinity Ward imploded.

Still, Sledgehammer tried to innovate again with its first solo title, Advanced Warfare. The game introduced exosuits, allowing players to jump, dash, and slide thanks to enhanced movement mechanics. It was a radical leap for Call of Duty, though fans largely rejected attempts to take the franchise into the future. Since then, Sledgehammer has played it fairly safe with two World War 2 games and a different game that also happened to be titled Modern Warfare 3, ironically enough.
Whether Sledgehammer Games can make something to excite fans again remains to be seen, but it'll be nice to have a non-MW or Black Ops game for the first time in more than five years.

news.title: World of Warcraft: Forever devs say gear upgrades will stay relevant 'for a long, long time': 'It's very much our intention to try wherever we can to not invalidate old content'
news.summary: Blizzard says items won't work like the modern version of the MMO.

others.title: Video: Digital Foundry Delivers Its Tech Review For Resident Evil 4 On Switch 2

content.v: The developers of World of Warcraft: Forever, the venerable MMO's newest 'Classic+' flavor, say that even though the level cap is staying at 60, there will always be new gear to chase, and lower level gear has never been more powerful.

Blizzard Entertainment developers are wary of the drastic increases in power in WoW's modern version, including the recent Midnight expansion, which render previous seasons of gear irrelevant, require massive resets between expansions and lead to periodic stat "squishes" to avoid players becoming omnipotent gods.

"Classic wasn't far off from this," vice president and senior game director Ion Hazzikostas said of Forever's approach in a recent PC Gamer interview. "It's gradual. Going from [Classic raids] Blackwing Lair to Ahn'Qiraj that's actually only a couple of item levels higher. Those two largely coexist. C'thun drops are probably better than anything in Blackwing Lair, but that's like one or two items per player. This is a system that can last for a long, long time."
Associate production director Clay Stone says that's part of what makes gear in Forever—and Classic—meaningful.
"Your best-in-slot that you pick up from a previous raid tier may continue to be your best in slot for a long time. It's very much our intention to try wherever we can to not invalidate old content."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/R2g2nfNeCoSe5bX8wvJYgY-1920-80.jpg
Then again, a long time isn't expected to be literally forever, Hazzikostas says.
"At some point, if you're running the Barrow Deeps raid that's coming out in December, you're going to have all the items that you want. That's fine. You're done with it."

Forever players will see gear progress at level 60: those modest item level increases, gear that's good in specific niche situations, and rare "chase" pieces should keep people hunting, Forever developers say.
An item might be especially powerful when fighting in a desert, or against a dragon, for example, making it particularly good in one especially tough fight.

(And yes, players, developers are aware that this means bag space will be at a premium. "We're already thinking about that," principal designer Kris Zierhut says, mentioning the ideas of more bank space, trinket bags or even garment bags to hold the excess.)
Un-solving the game
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TWf2yNegExMxJxn3T6vQ9Y-1920-80.jpg

Forever launches on November 4, and so far players have seen few of the pieces that will entice them at the end game. The current level cap in the beta is 30, and future items have been hidden from view and datamining to keep them guessing.

"We resurrected some old tech that keeps item stats and properties and tooltips secret, unknown to the client, until the item has actually been obtained by someone on the server," Hazzikostas says. "That's something we can use in modern WoW if we want."

Essentially a flag on items determines whether they are known, making them visible in the game's data. It trips when someone discovers an item for the first time, making sure that if the player links the item to others, it doesn't cause bugs

But until that moment, players can't get a sneak peek at what the piece of gear does. It's one reason why Forever doesn't have an Adventure Guide for dungeons; developers want the game to keep its secrets.

"Every single boss in our raids has some items that are very low percentage drop chase items, kind of like the Dragonspine Trophy was in Gruul's Lair—but for every boss," says Zierhut. "It might be three weeks, four weeks before somebody sees that item drop, and the whole meta is torn up again."
The goal is to keep the magic of exploration alive, he says.

"The goal is to un-solve the game, so players have to figure out again what's the best path," Zierhut says. "They don't know what the best items are. They don't know what to get. It's back to 2004 and nobody knows anything and figuring it out all over again."
Hand-crafted power
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Mxxu8paSa2qdYUVMb398kX-1920-80.jpg

To add a layer of complexity—and, again, keep players from gaining power too quickly—items deliberately aren't optimized for players' preferred classes and stats. "Our items are much more idiosyncratic, and you don't get exactly what you want," he says, noting that knowing your class and choosing between gear sets will be one way players express skill in Forever. "None of the gear is perfect."

That's an old strategy—there are oft-discussed items from WoW's original launch that put strength on cloth gear, for example—but what is new is how much power items can have at a relatively low level.
Both low-level drops and crafted gear are powerful early, and that's on purpose, developers say.

"A lot of times tradeskills felt like an afterthought in Classic. Like, 'Oh, I could craft this item, but it's too much work and I'm about to out-level it anyway. Skip it. I'll level up my tailor when I get to level 60,' " Zierhut says. "I made a deliberate effort to make more crafting recipes worthwhile to craft while you are leveling up, including lowering the skill requirement to craft them.

"The typical item from tailoring, leatherworking, blacksmithing requires 25 fewer skill points than it used to. So you'll be able to craft that item right around the time it's your best-in-slot at that level and get the real value out of doing it."
Much of the tuning done so far to gear in Forever's beta has been to keep that idea of modest but steady progression across the whole leveling process.
"It's just a slightly different gradient in terms of power level," lead game designer Tim Jones says.

news.title: A Massive Decompilation Community Is Shutting Down, Thanks to the Deluge of AI Decomps and Ports
news.summary: If you've been on gaming Twitter at all over the last month, you're probably aware of a massive wave of people

content.v: https://assets1.ignimgs.com/2021/03/01/halo-cortana-1614607712316.jpg

If you've been on gaming Twitter at all over the last month, you're probably aware of the massive wave of people using AI to rapidly decompile, port, and remix games. That wave of AI decomps has forced a massive decompilation community to sunset.

In a blog post, admin @encounter from decomp.dev , a community repository for people to track decompilation posts, cites a wave of bad actors who are using AI to essentially steal the hard work of programmers working on existing decompilation projects.

The act of decompiling games itself isn't new, and people have been taking games and trying to decompile them down to the source code for years. But what was once a herculean task requiring coding expertise can now be done with little effort thanks to new AI models like GPT 6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5.

The blog post doesn't blame the models themselves for the surge of vibe-coded decompilations and ports, but rather claims that bad actors are taking existing projects and then using AI to rush them to completion. While there might be some developers who are open to people with a Claude subscription using their work to create, say, a browser port of Halo , that should be up to each developer.

The post says, "Every project works differently: some may not want to use AI for legal or ethical reasons, and others may be okay with AI, or use AI themselves, but do not want drive-by contributions from folks who have put no effort into making sure the contributions are good. The bottom line is that these kinds of hostile forks put little to no effort into meaningfully contributing to existing projects, tearing apart our community fabric."

As for the ports themselves, the blog claims that people are taking the code from hobbyists and forcing a barely functioning port out of them. "While community members put in the effort to decompile a game, opportunists have frequently raced to release a half-baked, barely-functional port from it," @encounter writes.

The blog post also mentions that this recent wave of AI decomps, recomps, and ports is muddying the waters of what the decomp community is trying to do. A lot of classical decomps are done out of the love of games and a desire to know how they work, but this trend of using AI to brute force working PC ports has caused a lot of people to rush into communities like decomp.dev looking for simple ways to create easy PC ports of games.
As for decomp.dev itself, the website will still exist, and users can use it to track existing projects, but @encounter is taking down the main index and disabling new projects.

Unfortunately, when it comes to Opus 5.5, Astra 6, and decomps, the cat is out of the bag, and it's unlikely that one decomp repository going offline is going to meaningfully stop this trend. We've seen everything from making Minecraft playable on X/Twitter to modders shoving Minecraft and Elden Ring together . There have also been a lot of browser ports, with games like Halo: Combat Evolved and Grand Theft Auto 5 being briefly playable on Chrome before those games' respective publishers predictibly brought them crashing down.

Either way, it's a shame to see a community built out of the love of programming essentially die off because a bunch of people with Claude subscriptions are using game developers' work as a starting point and finishing it with AI.

news.title: CD Projekt Has Officially Begun Work on Project Hadar, but It's Not in Pre-Production Yet
news.summary: CD Projekt Red, the Polish developer best known for its amazing RPG series The Witcher and Cyberpunk 2077, has

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/15/cd-projekt-new-building-018-1792084979426.jpeg

CD Projekt Red, the Polish developer best known for its amazing RPG series The Witcher and Cyberpunk 2077 , has officially finished imagining up a new world for us to play in. The “world vision” stage for its new IP, Project Hadar, has been completed and work has officially begun on turning those concepts into a video game.

"This has been our biggest undertaking to date, taking us several years, but at this point we can say we have a coherent vision for this world and its key elements,” said Joint CEO Michał Nowakowski . “The team has begun work on the game, although it's not yet in pre-production.”

In September, CD Projekt Red said it was staffing up for Project Hadar, with a team over 30 strong with plans "to hire more, up to 50 developers by the end of this year. But what is it? In June, a new job advert teased what to expect , calling for an engineering director who would help “push the envelope for the next, immersive game in the Hadar world, creating an emotional, open-world experience that will stay with gamers.” Open-world confirmed!

CD Projekt Red is of course currently hard at work making The Witcher 4, which is the next game on the studio’s slate due out 2028. Before that, though, a third major expansion for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, titled Songs of the Past, is scheduled for release next year. Developed by Fool’s Theory, a team of former CD Projekt developers, the expansion aims to bridge the gap between The Witcher 3 and the next game in the series, starring Geralt’s adopted daughter, Ciri.

After that comes Cyberpunk 2, the follow-up to Cyberpunk 2077. And let's not forget that CD Projekt intends to release the new The Witcher 3 trilogy in the space of six years. Assuming CD Projekt hits 2028 for The Witcher 4, and the company sticks to its ambitious release strategy for this new The Witcher trilogy , we could see The Witcher 5 in 2031 and The Witcher 6 in 2034. Where Hadar fits in with all that is anyone's guess.

We know nothing about Project Hadar’s world or setting, but it’ll be cool to see what the wonderful minds at CDPR think up — especially as it’ll be designed first and foremost to support a sprawling RPG. I do selfishly wish CDPR would do one more license though. Give us a good Game of Thrones video game. Please. You could call it Project Hodor.

The next series of the anime based on CDPR and Pondsmith’s shared world is coming to Netflix on October 20. You can check out our interview with the creator of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 for the lowdown.

Elsewhere in CD Project Land, The Witcher 3 just got a remaster on consoles and PC, which saw the iconic RPG get a makeover to tide people over until the expansion. There were some issues with the new visuals, particularly heavy bloom in The Witcher 3 remaster , but CDPR fixed its prized goose sharpish.

news.title: Sega Pulls Total War: Shogun 2 Remaster After Backlash Over AI-Upscaled Graphics
news.summary: Following player backlash, Sega and Creative Assembly have yanked Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from

others.title: Sega Pulls Disastrous Total War: Shogun 2 Remaster From Sale Following Backlash

content.v: Following player backlash, Sega and Creative Assembly have yanked Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from sale and have replaced it with the original 2011 version. First hitting digital shelves on October 13, this version of the beloved strategy game was advertised as having had a substantial facelift, but it wasn't long before players pointed out numerous issues with the game and the telltale sign of AI-upscaling. This has led to some bizarre makeovers, like a samurai's face merging with his helmet or extra fingers on character artwork.

"We're aware that Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards," Sega wrote in a statement that did not address the AI criticisms at all. "We've seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be."

Fans have also taken to social media to show off legacy bugs that still haven't been addressed in this new edition, and Sega said that it's "working closely" with its "development partners" to identify and address these issues. Unsurprisingly, the game has an overwhelmingly negative rating on Steam currently, with over 81% of players urging people to give it a skip.

"Horrific graphical bug makes the vegetation in battle map terrible to look at. There's no way to disable the vegetation," one oddly specific player review reads," amongst hundreds of other negative pieces of feedback.

Players also weren't happy when Sega initially replaced the original Shogun 2 game with the remastered version, which has a price tag of $40. Upgrading from the classic to this version will cost you $10. The AI-upscaling is just the tip of the complaints-iceberg, as players have several other issues with Shogun 2. The new user interface has been criticized for its clunky design and plenty of new bugs have surfaced. This isn't the only game using generative AI that Sega is linked to, as for the upcoming Crazy Taxi: World Tour, generative AI was used to create background assets.

news.title: GTA 5 finally measures up to the actual best GTA game now I've added a jetpack

content.v: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .
World War 2 Canadian air force pilot John Gillespie Magee Jr once wrote, in his poem High Flight:
Oh! I have slipped the surly bonds of Earth And danced the skies on laughter-silvered wings; Sunward I've climbed, and joined the tumbling mirth of sun-split clouds,—and done a hundred things

He was talking about Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, his favourite game and an icon of the PS2 generation of consoles. In San Andreas, tucked away in the Verdant Meadows Airstrip, the player could locate a jetpack, and tumble through the skies of Las Venturas like a glorious errant star. GTA 5? No jetpack. This is why it's an inferior game.

Until now. I have installed Aerowing - Wearable Jet Pack & Weapon System . Or, well, I installed it, tried to launch the game, crashed my PC, rebooted, tried to launch the game, crashed the game, rebooted, then launched the game.

It's a strangely lavish mod, I'll give it that. You don't just tap F and sort of limply ascend, which is mostly how it went in San Andreas. No, you get a whole animation, the camera circles your guy as he does a possibly-copyrighted Iron Man pose and launches himself skywards.
Then off you go, a speedometer in the corner measuring your courage as you glide along, launching one of three weapons: SMG, plasma, and "tube," which I'm pretty sure is just SMG again.

It's a rollocking good time, and it'll be even better once I find a way to proc it that doesn't also proc my street golfing mod. Until then, with silent lifting mind I'll tread the high untrespassed sanctity of space, put out my hand, and touch the face of God.

news.title: 33 New Details From the GTA 6 Launch Trailer
news.summary: GTA 6's launch trailer may only be 90 seconds long, but there's plenty to see - here's the 33 details we spott

others.title: 10 Things We Noticed In The GTA 6 Launch Trailer

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/15/gta-launch-details-blog-1792081847737.jpg

Yet another look at GTA 6 has come our way, which means it’s time to get forensic; we’ve gone through the new trailer with a fine-tooth comb to pick out all of the interesting details hidden within. From peeks at what’s in store for some of its most explosive missions, further insights into Jason’s military past, and more than one visit to a steamy shower, there’s plenty of new things to take a look at.
Let’s not waste any more time. Here are the 33 details we spotted in the GTA 6 launch trailer.

Multiple shots offer a closer look at Jason and paint a pretty clear picture of the kind of man we’ll be taking control of. We already knew that he was ex-military, but midway through the trailer we see him wearing a U.S. Army T-shirt that offers more details on his service.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/15/1-1792081397126.jpg

1. Firstly, the combat training school Jason seemingly trained at is located in North Fort Law. Longtime fans will recognise this as the military base from the very first Grand Theft Auto game. In that original game, it was located in the state of New Guernsey, but it’s more likely that the one Jason attended is in the State of Alderney, the HD universe’s take on New Jersey. We know that Lucia is from Liberty City, which is located in the neighboring State of Liberty – perhaps they met when Jason was stationed at the base?

2. More prominent than that small print is the word “Marauder,” which matches the skull-and-parachute tattoo on Jason’s arm that we’ve seen in previous videos. The Marauders are presumably the unit he served in, and may be a reference to the real-life Merrill's Marauders, a 1940s special forces group. Its modern-day equivalent is the 75th Ranger Regiment, and so it’s likely that Jason was a ranger.

3. It seems like Jason has fallen on tough times since he left the forces. “I got in some trouble in the army, didn’t leave on the best of terms,” he says in the trailer’s opening. “They don’t give loans, anything, to people like me.” With a situation like that, it’s no wonder Jason has resorted to crime. The cost of living is only going up!
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/15/2-1792081421431.jpg

4. Thankfully, it seems like Jason’s experience in the Marauders has equipped him with all the tools for a very fruitful life of crime. We see him wading through water dressed in special forces-like infiltration gear, a pair of night-vision goggles on his head and a silenced assault rifle in his hands. He’s accompanied by two other men, and the trio seem to have disembarked from a boat. While the blush night sky certainly looks very Floridian (or should we say Leonidan), an odd reptile to the left of the scene appears to be a komodo dragon, which is native to Indonesia. Is this a flashback to a mission from Jason’s army days? Or is the reptile simply a native of Leonida’s wetlands, and Jason has perhaps called on some former squadmates to help with some kind of job?

5. Much of the criminal work we see committed across this trailer has something of a military feel to it. We later see Jason on a helicopter, dressed in a bulletproof vest and demonstrating a very professional demeanor. He’s joined by a dog, potentially pointing to not just Jason having a pet, but also being able to use them as some kind of working dog. Later shots also show Jason confidently disembarking a chopper and checking the chambered round in his rifle – all small details, but ones that help paint the picture of a deeply competent professional.

6. Lucia may not have Jason’s highly trained background, but it looks like she’ll eventually adopt at least some of his tactics. A minute into the trailer, we can see her dressed in special forced black and equipped with a Shrewsbury rotary grenade launcher, popping explosives into pursuing police vehicles.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/15/3-1792081441492.jpg

7. She’s demolishing those cars from on high, hanging from the side of some kind of cargo net. A few seconds later, we see a helicopter carrying a giant load in a very similar cargo net – it seems likely that these shots are taken from the same mission, and that Lucia will hang from the net before or after it’s been dragged through the side of a skyscraper.

8. The damage caused by the crash is more detailed than anything we’ve seen in prior GTA games, with hundreds of shards of glass erupting from the side of the building. While this shot alone is far from confirmation that the game will feature Battlefield-like destruction tech, it is a flashy insight into just how detailed Rockstar is able to make environmental demolition.

9. That kind of collateral damage is to be expected from crime on the scale that GTA typically depicts, and it seems like this game has no intention of being smaller than GTA 5’s biggest moments. We can see Lucia leaping off a car onto a commercial liner, suggesting something on the same scale as some of Trevor’s airborne antics. This shot is likely the precursor to the scene in the second trailer that shows Lucia fighting in a plane’s hold as its landing gear deploys.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/15/4-1792081458953.jpg

10. The aforementioned chopper mission is probably a heist, but what’s definitely a heist is the bank job we see. This is actually the vault we previously saw in a screenshot we exclusively debuted back in August , complete with the burning bank notes and Lucia with her hair in a ponytail.

11. For that shot, Lucia is joined not by Jason but by another anonymous character. We can’t see their face, but whoever they are, it looks like we won’t be alone when conducting heists. In a later shot we see Lucia accompanied by gunmen disguised as construction workers, suggesting we’ll often be joined by crews of criminals. But will these be supporting characters introduced as part of the story, or NPCs hired to help, akin to how heist crews worked in GTA 5?

12. While stealing physical money is a tried and tested form of securing dosh, there’s a chance that GTA 6 will toy with a more decentralised approach, too. We see a bi-plane flying over Vice City’s beach, its side emblazoned with the logo for “DacityCoin.” That’s presumably some kind of Bitcoin parody, but why is it so prominent in the trailer? Why is there a guy hanging onto the plane’s wing and deploying a bright pink smoke flare? Our theory is that Jason and Lucia will take part in some kind of scam, and this is a stunt to advertise a bogus cryptocurrency.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/15/5-1792081479051.jpg
13. Planes aren’t the only high-speed thrills on show. A little later we see street racing, a side activity we first saw in August’s extended look.

14. Of course, most of GTA’s high-speed driving tends to be a race against the cops. A short car chase sequence sees one of our protagonists behind the wheel of a lime green supercar, fleeing police that arrive from all angles. It seems like every new trailer shows off new cars, and we get a very quick peek at the new Invetero Coquette, which can be glimpsed for a split second – look out for its turquoise-and-pink synthwave paint job.

15. For those who prefer waves to asphalt, you might find more joy in the Shasa, which appears to be a new model of boat for GTA 6. We can see Jason and his buddy Cal working on one, buffing out the paintwork. This seems to be Jason’s reality at the start of the story – with his army days behind him, he’s working as a laborer at Brian’s Marina.

content.v: Upcoming Pokemon x Razer Viper V4 Pro https://t.co/qsAKwBhcg8 October 15, 2026

For a company that has made the best mouse I've ever laid my hands on, it sure seems to be doing its darndest to destroy that mystique. I think it looks bloody awful. There's just something about that peculiar mix of grey, yellow, and green that seems very uncoordinated. Why can't a good thing be left alone? The Viper V4 Pro is fantastic, and that's in part because it looks sleek and simple, and because it's cheaper than other top-end gaming mice from big brands.
There's a chair, too, and a keyboard, which my colleague James says he prefers the look of to the mouse. I think I agree, but I still think the the grey clashes too much with the green.
Back to the Viper, though, there could have been a chance here to make a proper red-and-white, pokeball-themed version, but instead we get this grey-and-whatever-else monstrosity.
I'll just keep hold of the white one, thank you very much.

news.title: The AI bubble may not have burst yet, but $1 trillion worth of air appears to have escaped
news.summary: Not so much 'going out with a bang' as 'anticlimactic party balloon deflation'.

content.v: Many of tech's heaviest hitters have seen their share prices decrease significantly this week. For instance, Nvidia has seen a decrease of about 8% over the last five days—and this AI company is far from the only one seeing such a dip.

Over the last five days, we've seen share prices fall by 13% for AMD, and nearly 15% for Intel. Looking more broadly across the AI and semiconductor industries, CNBC reports 20 of the most valuable players have shed more than $1 trillion in value as investors sell off stock.
The bigger picture doesn't look any better: over the last five days, Samsung Electronics has seen its share price decrease by nearly 20%, SK hynix is down 18%, and Micron has seen a dip of over 15%.

A combination of factors have likely triggered this big chip stock sell off, including concerns that the memory supply crisis may actually reverse into oversupply come 2029, according to a recent column in South Korea's Maeil Business Newspaper .

There's more going on than just the CEO of Acer insisting " It's impossible for the shortage to last until 2030 !" We also know that many chip manufacturers have already been working to boost their production capacity, though TSMC's next-gen Arizona fab is fully booked before it has even been built .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/gZVF2aBShFnje6vinn5PvR-1920-80.jpg

Chinese manufacturer CXMT is also growing, which is likely to go at least some way towards putting a dampener on the western market's aspirations. It's been stocking up on western DUV machines and is estimated to match Micron in terms of DRAM manufacturing capabilities this year . The chip manufacturer also recently claimed it had created breakthrough chip architecture that increases memory density . Make no mistake, CXMT is one to watch.

On top of that, The CEOs of both Intel and Broadcom recently claimed that financing could become a bigger hurdle to overcome for the AI industry than even securing memory or electricity supply. The uptick in interest rates means that investors may feel the balance between borrowing and the return on investment for big tech's data centre build out is looking increasingly lopsided.

So, is the AI bubble finally popping? Even as air is clearly escaping, it's still hard to say. The resulting lower share prices from this widespread stock sell-off may inspire some investors to buy, for one thing.

Despite the high price of these infrastructure projects, the demand for AI computing remains robust according to tech analyst Dan Ives for merchant bank Yorkville Ives. Ives told CNBC, "What would change our view is a demand signal, not [an increased interest] rate signal."
As such, big tech likely won't be ditching data centres any time soon, and the AI bubble may once again reach for something more party-balloon shaped in the future.

news.title: How WoW: Forever Is “Pushing The Envelope,” And What Comes After Launch
news.summary: It's not often one of the biggest games of all time gets a do-over. It's even rarer for a game to get a third

content.v: It's not often one of the biggest games of all time gets a do-over. It's even rarer for a game to get a third attempt. But that, in many ways, is what World of Warcraft: Forever is.

Developer Blizzard is pulling from 22 years of hindsight for what is the third major version of its landmark MMORPG, set to launch on November 4. That two-decade span includes not only the release of 11 WoW expansions, but also the re-release of the original WoW in 2019 and its subsequent "classic" expansions, as well. In the years since WoW Classic's launch, Blizzard has gone from "no changes" to "some changes," taking lessons learned from each Classic release and using them to inform their future work.

With WoW: Forever, Blizzard is finally going beyond replicating history and is instead forging a new vision for its genre-defining MMO, even if that vision is one firmly rooted in the past. GameSpot recently had the chance to talk with Clay Stone, associate production director on WoW: Forever, and Holly Longdale, executive producer and VP for WoW, about how Blizzard approached making a "new" version of original WoW, its approach to Forever's endgame, and what players can expect from Forever's future.
Exceeding Expectations

From the outset, Stone said Blizzard wanted to "push the envelope" and make a big first impression with Forever that went beyond players' expectations. Players certainly had a lot of them. The idea of a new version of WoW Classic that preserved the original game's world but added new content is one that's been around for a long time, and with it all kinds of community ideas of what it should and shouldn't be.

That made it important for Blizzard to deliver not just what players wanted, but go even further, Stone said. Rather than just class-balance changes or the completion of some of WoW's original unfinished quests and zones, as many players likely expected, Blizzard instead went bigger. It created over 1,000 new quests, four new zones, thousands of new items, substantial class changes, multiple new gameplay systems, and even an unexpected playable race not seen in any other version of WoW, Skyborne elves.

"I think that it was important for us to do this up front, to basically not have everything feel like, 'Oh, I predicted that …' and do that now rather than not do that and wait five years down the line," Stone said.
Waiting years to bring a new race or other major additions would be too late, Stone said.

"If there's an opportunity for us to take some bigger swings and some bigger risks up front, I think it sets us up much better for the long-term health of the game and figuring out ways for us to be able to create new surprises for players," he said.

In fact, Blizzard originally planned even more new additions for Forever's launch. Stone said Blizzard scaled some of those plans back as the game got further into development and its announcement at BlizzCon 2026 loomed. Stone teased more new race and class combos than what are currently playable on the game's beta, as well as "more extreme" class changes as seen in WoW Classic's Season of Discovery, could be coming to Forever in the future.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image_9f78b2.jpeg?w=636

Blizzard is "deliberately holding back just a little" on what's to come, he said. At BlizzCon, it announced a roadmap through Summer 2027 that included new raids, dungeons, and quests, as well as the launch of the game's "Hardcore" permadeath server.

"As we got closer [to BlizzCon], I think we did start to get a lot smarter and go, 'Okay, let's go ahead and draw the line here. You know, this is a lot. This is great for launch.' But it also allows us to save some really good stuff in terms of new content, new dungeons, new raids--things like that--new race/class combos, for not that far after launch," Stone said.
Staying On Azeroth

What some of that new content will be is the subject of wild speculation among the game's passionate community. Stone was adamant the team is committed to "staying on Azeroth" and that there's "a lot of [existing] space [on the original world map] that we already know about and we have plans for."

When asked if Forever would potentially take players to areas outside Azeroth's original two continents of Kalimdor and Eastern Kingdoms, including places seen in other WoW expansions, Stone said the world is a big place and that there are "other locations on Azeroth that are not necessarily Eastern Kingdoms or Kalimdor that we may want to go visit in the future."

"I think that the creative constraint of telling ourselves we're going to stay on Azeroth has created some really cool and interesting creative opportunities for us to explore some places that perhaps players have seen before, and perhaps some places that they haven't seen before," he said.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image_4c9682.jpeg?w=636

As for what else the future may hold, Blizzard is already surveying the community on potential new classes , which raises the natural question of how Forever will be monetized going forward. The game is included as part of WoW's $15 monthly subscription, as has always been the case with WoW Classic, but for the first time Blizzard is charging $30 for a new race, the Skyborne. While previous WoW expansions have added new races and classes for a price, those expansions have also come with whole new worlds to explore and gameplay systems to master. In the case of the Skyborne, they do come with a new starting zone, but it's hardly an entire expansion's worth of new content.

Longdale said charging for access to the Skyborne was an example of Blizzard "testing things out" and finding a way to "support the team and support the business" without adding "unnecessary barriers" for players accustomed to being able to play WoW Classic with their subscription. It's not necessarily a confirmed business model for how Blizzard will handle the addition of new content in the future, she said. It's also not an indication that Blizzard is planning on "throwing a bunch of new races" into the game, though she said there's "a lot of stuff on the table" when it comes to possibilities.
"It's just something we're trying right now," Longdale said. "We'll see if players like it and if it's a reasonable model going forward."
Launch Is Just The Start

Even as players speculate about Forever's future, there are still plenty of unknowns pertaining to the game's launch. Players have only been able to reach level 30 in the game's beta, and there are still thousands of "secret" items in the game's files yet to be discovered.

Forever's endgame raids will unlock on December 9 for those who have reached level 60 roughly a month after launch, but what those raids will entail, and the items hidden within them, is still a mystery. Unlike in original WoW, where items gained from subsequent raid tiers represented substantial leaps in player power, Stone said Blizzard is aiming to make power progression between raid tiers in Forever "as compact as possible" while still making new raids "fulfilling and desirable."

He said one aspect about WoW Classic the Forever team loves is being able to find powerful, best-in-slot items from endgame dungeons or the world itself. Stone said there are "a lot of opportunities" for that tradition to continue in Forever, and that there are some "unannounced" ideas the team has that aim to keep content like dungeons relevant so that players will want to return to them. Combined with new additions like the Legacy system, an account-wide perk tree that rewards players for leveling up different classes, mastering new professions, and exploring the world, Stone said the intent is for it to never be too late to jump into Forever.

news.summary: Sega admits Shogun 2 - Complete Edition "has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards," so

content.v: Just two days after the disastrous release of Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition, Sega says it is removing the game from sale and putting the original back until it gets things sorted out.
WHAT HAPPENED:

Which brings us to now: After two days of silence, Sega has finally made a move: It says "the current experience is not where it needs to be," and is thus "working with platform holders to remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YbBwxHQxXATzJ6j5GUCZv7-1920-80.jpg
Anyone who purchased Shogun 2 - Complete Edition will still have access to it, but how (or if) Sega will enable them to go back to playing the original version wasn't clarified.

Pulling Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from sale and restoring the original is obviously the right move, and today's message promises improvements to the game to bring it more in-line with expectations, so hopefully we'll see some of the more glaring bugs and QoL issues resolved.

But all of this is still a very bad look for Creative Assembly, which has had something of an up-and-down history with its games and players over the years. It's a particular shame coming so soon after the company's successful launch of the Lords of the End Times expansion for Total War: Warhammer, which has been widely praised.

The announcement of Total War: Warhammer 40k also has a lot of RTS fans, and WH40K sickos, very excited, and nonsense like this really takes the wind out of those sails: If Shogun 2 - Complete Edition allowed out the door in this condition, how are fans supposed to expect better in the future?
A few fans have also pointed out that in 2024, Sega's Aegis-CWA union accused the company of outsourcing Q&A and some localization services, resulting in the layoffs of 61 people.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/6qKFAEnvbfR8eLZSsFcSoS-1920-80.png

As I write this, Shogun 2 - Complete Edition remains available for purchase on Steam , GOG , and the Epic Games Store —Sega has not specified when it will be removed. It has also not yet responded to the accusations of gen AI usage in Shogun 2 - Complete Edition—I've reached out to ask about that and will update if I receive a reply.

news.title: Diablo 5 Inches Closer to Launch as Cinematics Work Begins
news.summary: Diablo 5 is still a few years away, but it looks like development is trucking along, now that Blizzard has sta

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/15/d5-1792078974394.jpg
Diablo 5 is still a few years away , but it looks like development is trucking along, now that Blizzard has started filming for its cinematics.

Blizzard cinematic director Neil David Carter posted a photo of the motion capture stage on X / Twitter , simply saying "First shoot #Diablo5." If the cinematic team is just starting motion capture, Diablo 5 probably isn't super late in its development. However, if the cinematic team is shooting motion capture for cutscenes, then the story is mostly fleshed out already.

Luckily, in an interview with Windows Central, senior producer Tiffany Watt confirmed that Diablo 5 would be using its own fork of the Diablo 4 engine, so at least the team didn't have to start building the game from scratch. But in a game like Diablo 5, a lot of work has to go into balance, itemization and world design, and the new game is likely going to be a bit more complicated than Diablo 4 thanks to the procedurally generated maps.
First shoot #Diablo5 https://t.co/3SDU51n3ch

That's why some folks, like former co-founder of Path of Exile developer Grinding Gear Games , are skeptical that Diablo 5 is going to hit its targeted release date. After all, if Diablo 5 does launch in spring 2029, it will come out just shy of six years after Diablo 4. There was an 11-year gap between Diablo 3 and Diablo 4. The gap between Diablo 4 and Diablo 5, if all goes according to plan, will be about half as long. It's little wonder, then, that Blizzard has had to work hard to convince its players that it's not abandoning Diablo 4 early, and that the game will still get content even after Diablo 5 launches .

Only time will be able to tell whether or not Diablo 4 will continue to get updates, or will just get a handful of seasons on repeat like Diablo 3 after Diablo 4 launched. But, really, all we can do is wait and see how everything plays out. For what it's worth, Diablo 5 is shaping up to be a totally different ARPG than its predecessor, and I can't wait to see how the cinematics they're shooting now are going to turn out.

Diablo 5 will tell 'three stories,' including the past, the present desolation of Diablo's takeover, and the future 'terror forming' of Sanctuary. Diablo 5 is set roughly one century after Diablo 4, in a post-apocalyptic timeline where the Lord of Terror himself has already won and rules over a fallen Sanctuary.

news.title: 79% of you think Razer's new gaming mouse feature counts as cheating
news.summary: I doubt it will do a 180, though. Hey-hey!

content.v: Last week, I asked whether Razer's "Perfect 180" feature on its new Basilisk V4 Pro gaming mouse counts as cheating . For the unaware, said feature allows a near-instant 180-degree spin to be mapped within the software to a single mouse button. In other words, one click, one insta-turn to face whatever (or whoever) is behind you.
316 of you responded to the poll (where were the rest, asleep?), and the results are... unsurprising. 79% of respondents said yes, while 21% said no, it's totally fine.
Does Razer's "Perfect 180" gaming mouse feature count as cheating?
Out of 316 poll respondents, here are the results expressed as percentages:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bkwSqn4ocKYaQwBeFt2HHb.png
Or just "no." I'm adding a bit of flavour to that one. Looking through the comments, many seemed to echo the sentiments of TrexLaser, who says: "Anything that moves the mouse for you is cheating."

However, some took a more nuanced approach. Terito697174 says the real issue might be in the determination of cheaters, as overly snappy aiming is often the only way for another player to reasonably assess whether they're up against an opponent with an unfair advantage.
Salvador Pardiñas makes a good point: "I can sort of understand it as an accessibility option for people who can't normally do a 180 by themselves, but other than that it's just plain cheating."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Ujo3PEQou798FVRe7VgoMD-1920-80.jpg

Certainly, those with differing abilities might find a 180 turn on a mouse button a very useful thing indeed. However, that doesn't seem to be the way Razer is currently pitching it, as the feature blurb on the Basilisk V4 Pro product page describes it as "built for low-sensitivity gaming," rather than as an accessibility option.
Commenter Fojacko brings up a real blast from the past: "Welcome to the 2000s, Razer. The Intellipoint software says hi."

I'd forgotten all about Microsoft's SideWinder gaming mice from back in the day, which, via the Intellipoint mouse software , could reassign a side button to perform 180-degree or full 360-degree turns. "Quick turn never took off back then for a reason," says Fojacko. Erm, I'm not quite sure why. Was it not as useful as we might think?

Anyway, the feelings of the majority have been made clear. I doubt Razer will rescind the feature regardless, but I will definitely be looking out for insta-turning players in multiplayer games from now on.
"I know what mouse you use," I'll think to myself. Also, "How on earth am I supposed to compete with that?"

news.title: A New Call Of Duty Sub-Series Is Coming, After Years Of Black Ops and Modern Warfare
news.summary: Activision chief marketing officer Tyler Bahl has confirmed that a new sub-series is on the way for Call of Du

content.v: Activision chief marketing officer Tyler Bahl has confirmed that a new sub-series is on the way for Call of Duty . Modern Warfare 4 is just over a week away from launching (though campaign early access starts tomorrow) and marks the fifth straight year of either a Black Ops or Modern Warfare entry in the franchise. That looks set to change going forward.

Speaking with The Game Business , Bahl elaborated on why Activision won't do back-to-back sequels in the same sub-series . "[The Call of Duty community] wanted something fresh, and even though there were different time settings, and ways to play the game with new features, that tonal shift is something that they were looking for. So, we've already stated that a future title is going to be a new sub-franchise, and we've already laid the groundwork."

Last month, Black Ops developer Treyarch teased that it's working on "something that nobody's ever experienced before." Meanwhile, Sledgehammer Games is reportedly in charge of 2027's Call of Duty , which might also introduce a new sub-series for Call of Duty. The last game in the franchise to not be a Black Ops or Modern Warfare entry was 2021's Vanguard--created by Sledgehammer. So there is precedent there for the studio.

In addition, Activision is now in charge of the Halo franchise . Xbox management is stating that a new team will be spun up for the new Halo game, but it wouldn't be surprising to see a Call of Duty studio being heavily involved.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 comes out October 23 on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch 2. Preordering the FPS unlocks campaign early access for tomorrow, October 16, as well as the DMZ mode on October 20.

news.title: ‘I Can Really Nitpick Things’ – Firearms Expert Jonathan Ferguson Explains the Most Common Gun Mistakes in Games
news.summary: We spoke to the internet's favorite firearms expert, Jonathan Ferguson, about all the things games get wrong a

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/14/jonathanfergusonguns-blogroll-1791984347541.jpeg

Hell Let Loose: Vietnam has a familiar voice hiding in its loadout menu. Click on any gun or grenade and you can listen to an audio description voiced by none other than Jonathan Ferguson, Keeper of Firearms and Artillery at the Royal Armouries Museum in Leeds . Ferguson has become something of a cult figure at the intersection of firearms history and video games, thanks to his detailed breakdowns of video game weapons on YouTube, but he also now plays a part in the development of video games, thanks to the Royal Armouries' consultation service. He’s worked with studios such as Team17, Facepunch, and Rebellion to ensure their weapons are as accurate as possible and avoid commonly-made mistakes, such as getting shotguns completely wrong.

"The most persistent [mistake] that you still occasionally see is shotguns being completely less than lethal, or non-lethal, even, at a set distance," Ferguson tells me, although he does note that “I think a lot of developers have wised up on this.”

It's certainly true that the years of shotguns effectively being little more than loud knives is drawing to a close, across not only mil-sims but blockbusters, too. Both Insurgency: Sandstorm and Red Dead Redemption 2 are notable for their more realistic depictions of shotguns.
"The more and more detail we see incorporated in games, the more they're able to make it resemble reality a bit more,” Ferguson tells me.

There are few people better-equipped to answer a developer’s questions about firearms than Ferguson, who not only reacts to in-game guns for the EXP YouTube channel but is also a gamer himself. His understanding of the needs of gameplay over raw historical accuracy made him an ideal fit for consulting on Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, although developer Expression Games’ realistic depiction of shotguns with authentic (even slightly generous) range is less to do with his consultancy than the studio doing its homework across the era’s entire arsenal.
“I didn't need to tell them that the K50M submachine gun existed and was specific to the North Vietnamese,” explains Ferguson. “They already knew that. So they'd done their due diligence there."

Beyond the shotgun issue, Ferguson often finds himself picking up on minutiae. "There are lots of little tiny details, like realistic patterns of cartridge case ejection for example,” he tells me, “which really don't matter to how the game is played, but if you notice them, adds to it.”

Through his appearances on Firearms Expert Reacts videos, Ferguson has built a reputation for picking apart the details many players won’t even notice. And so in the matter of case ejection patterns, he recognises there’s a bigger picture.

“There is a difference between criticising or observing, reacting, and actually playing,” he says. “There are a number of games where either I've played them previously and then I'm being asked to comment on them, or I haven't played them yet but I do later, and I realise, ‘oh that thing I commented on, I didn't notice at all’, because my attention is where it should be: on the gameplay, the story, the enemies, whatever."

Increased visual fidelity is something of a double-edged sword when it comes to these kind of problems. During the the days of Doom and Quake, no one expected ejecting shells to be animated to reflect reality. Today, when so many items in games are rendered to reflect real-world physics, we expect to see something more realistic.

"That's the kind of level of detail we're at,” says Ferguson. “I can really nitpick things, and it gets increasingly hard to actually nitpick that stuff [because the detail has become so good]. Occasionally, I find out that's because of something I've said, which is kind of rewarding, but I also feel bad because it's making people do extra work."

Sometimes, the quest for realism can require games to become less realistic to feel just right. Ferguson explains that pistol slides are a good example of this – in video games, it’s better if they move much slower than they do in reality.

"If you can see them moving, that showcases the animator's skill. Things aren't clipping through each other and it looks cool,” he explains. “In reality, if you shoot a gun, even if you stare right at that moving part, you can't really see it move. It's kind of faster than your eye can realistically perceive.

“But [a player’s] expectation is, 'well I know that bit of a gun moves', and [if] they don't see something move, or it moves really fast and they can't really tell, they might think, 'oh, that's not very satisfying'."
The Real Meta
Ferguson himself also wasn't immune to a misplaced sense of realism during his youth, years before he became an expert at the Royal Armouries.

"I'll never forget firing up GoldenEye 64 for the first time,” he says. “Something about the way the AK was represented in that, the sound of it, the muzzle flash, the way you could sort of wave it about, that felt so much like, ‘oh, that's like a real rifle.’
“Of course, it's not at all,” he adds. “Especially when you look in third person, it looks like they're just one-handing the thing. But in ‘97, that was super impressive."

GoldenEye's version of the AK-47 may not have been realistic, but the assault rifle it is based on occupies a unique position in popular culture. It has become a symbol as much as a weapon, used and recognised across the entire planet. If anything has achieved the status of “meta” in the real world, as weapons do in games, it’s the AK-47.

"That distinctive profile, especially with the steeply curved magazine of the 7.62x39 original version, is an absolute icon,” Ferguson says. “A literal icon. I don't use ‘iconic’ in the lazy way, I use it in a literal way, because it appears on the flag of Mozambique for this very reason. It's a tool of liberation for some, a tool of terrorism and violence for others."

Of course, move across the globe to Europe and North America and there’s another assault rifle that could claim the same thing. "I think certainly the Western world would say AR-15,” he says. “A short-barreled AR-15 with a telescopic stock and a flat top. That's kind of the go-to for all sorts of people."

While “meta” has a deeper meaning, it’s often perceived as “the popular weapon everyone uses”, and what’s popular in one medium can directly influence what’s used in another. Ferguson’s deep knowledge of firearms, video games, and pop-culture means he’s able to spot how one medium’s fascination with a certain weapon creates a sort of “feedback loop”. One particularly notable example is the use of "the specific chopped, converted HK94 that was used in several ‘80s action movies, including, most famously, Die Hard" in the GTA games.

But while movies have long had a widespread influence on video games, Ferguson notes that the tide is somewhat turning: "Games have been in the shadow of movies, but I think they've moved beyond it." The first example that he reaches for doesn’t have anything to do with guns at all, but Ferguson notes that Spider-Man: Brand New Day uses "fight scenes and finishing moves taken from the Insomniac games. Obviously, that was the inspiration. I think we'll see that with guns as well."

news.title: GTA 5 Will Be Removed From PS Plus Just Before GTA 6 Releases, It Seems
news.summary: One of the biggest games that PlayStation Plus subscribers can play as part of their membership is Rockstar's

content.v: One of the biggest games that PlayStation Plus subscribers can play as part of their membership is Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 5. However, the game will reportedly get yanked from the service soon, just ahead of GTA 6 's release.

People on Reddit say they have received a notification telling them that GTA 5 will be removed for Extra and Premium subscribers on November 17. That is two days before GTA 6 launches on November 19, so the timing certainly suggests Sony and Rockstar are trying to migrate people to the new game.

The notice also includes a link directing people to the preorder page for GTA 6. "Whether you've yet to experience the tale of Franklin, Michael, and Trevor, or want to revisit it before Jason and Lucia's Vice City story begins, now's the time," Sony's notice said.
GTA 5 has rotated in and out of Xbox Game Pass over the years as well, and it is not currently available through the service.

GTA 6 launches on November 19, and the game's steamy launch trailer just arrived . The trailer was stuffed with exciting new details, so be sure to read up on GameSpot's 10 things we noticed from the GTA 6 launch trailer .
